package_info.why_malicious: The Jackson library has historically contained multiple high-severity vulnerabilities, most notably deserialization of untrusted data, which can allow attackers to execute arbitrary code or manipulate application logic by sending crafted payloads to the deserializer. These vulnerabilities are critical because they can be exploited remotely and affect a wide range of applications using Jackson for JSON/XML processing.

execution_context.file_location: Application code using Jackson's ObjectMapper.readValue() or similar methods
required_permissions: filesystem (if deserialized objects interact with files)
network (if deserialized objects perform network actions)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
ObjectMapper mapper = new ObjectMapper();
Object obj = mapper.readValue(untrustedInput, Object.class);
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code deserializes attacker-controlled input using ObjectMapper.readValue(), allowing instantiation of arbitrary classes and execution of their methods, which can result in remote code execution or unauthorized manipulation of application state.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deserializing untrusted data without enforcing type restrictions or input validation enables attackers to supply crafted payloads that exploit known gadget chains, leading to arbitrary code execution within the application context.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior expects deserialization to only instantiate safe, explicitly allowed classes from trusted sources. Malicious behavior occurs when attacker-controlled data triggers instantiation of dangerous or unexpected classes, violating application security boundaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Deserializing trusted, validated data from known sources with strict type controls is legitimate and expected in many business applications.
key_indicators: Deserialization of untrusted or user-supplied data
Use of ObjectMapper.readValue() on input not validated or type-restricted
Absence of explicit type whitelisting or input sanitization
Instantiation of classes outside the expected application domain during deserialization

execution_context.file_location: Application code using Jackson's XmlMapper.readValue() or similar methods
required_permissions: network (if XXE payloads trigger external requests)
filesystem (if XXE payloads access local files)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
XmlMapper xmlMapper = new XmlMapper();
Object obj = xmlMapper.readValue(untrustedXml, Object.class);
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code deserializes attacker-controlled XML input using XmlMapper.readValue(), which may process XML External Entity (XXE) payloads, enabling attackers to read local files or initiate server-side request forgery (SSRF) via crafted XML entities.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Parsing untrusted XML without disabling external entity resolution allows XXE attacks, which can exfiltrate sensitive files or perform SSRF by causing the application to make arbitrary network requests.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal XML parsing should explicitly disable external entity resolution when handling untrusted input to prevent access to local files or internal network resources. Malicious behavior occurs when this protection is absent, exposing the application to XXE exploitation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Parsing trusted XML data with external entities enabled may be legitimate for specific business logic, but should never be used with untrusted or user-supplied XML.
key_indicators: XML parsing of untrusted or user-supplied input
No explicit disabling of external entity resolution in XmlMapper configuration
Potential for file or network access via XML entity expansion
Outbound network requests or file reads triggered during XML deserialization

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted JSON or XML payload to an application endpoint that uses Jackson for deserialization.
Application deserializes the payload using ObjectMapper or XmlMapper, instantiating attacker-specified classes or resolving external XML entities.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution, file read, or SSRF

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains remote code execution, exfiltrates files, or performs further attacks within the application context.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromise of application and potential lateral movement

behavioral_signatures: Deserialization of untrusted data using ObjectMapper.readValue() or XmlMapper.readValue() without type restrictions
Instantiation of unexpected or dangerous classes during deserialization processes
Parsing of XML input with external entity resolution enabled, especially from user-supplied sources
file_indicators: Application code invoking ObjectMapper.readValue() or XmlMapper.readValue() on untrusted or user-supplied input
Lack of explicit type whitelisting or input validation in deserialization routines
Absence of XmlMapper configuration to disable external entity resolution
network_indicators: Outbound network requests initiated during XML parsing (indicative of XXE or SSRF exploitation)
Unexpected connections to internal or external resources triggered by deserialization of attacker-supplied data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Perform static analysis to identify application code that deserializes untrusted input using Jackson's ObjectMapper or XmlMapper without type restrictions or input validation. Flag code paths where XmlMapper is used without disabling external entity resolution. Monitor runtime behavior for instantiation of unexpected classes during deserialization and for outbound network requests or file access patterns triggered by XML parsing. Use dynamic monitoring to detect exploitation attempts, such as XXE payloads causing file reads or SSRF.
